text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
COFFEE - COFFEE: World market for February 27, 1997

Robusta futures in London pulled back from an earlier advance but ended with pared losses. There was no new market moving news and traders said the market remained vulnerable to further sharp swings on the back of fluctuating arabica futures in New York. Most active May was chased up to high of $1,635 a tonne before falling to a $1,550 floor as New York faltered after a higher start.

Traders said the slide in London accelerated after May triggered stop loss selling at below $1,580, the closing level on Wednesday. Uncovered positions on spot March, which enters the first delivery day on Monday, continued to decline as origins continued price- fixing and players rolled forward positions.
Arabica futures in New York pulled back slightly, one day after climbing to their highest levels in two years, as speculators took profits on the market's sweeping rally, trade sources said.

Prices shot higher at the opening on momentum from Wednesday's 10-cent rise, but the buying interest faded before the market could test new life-of-contract highs. The market then retreated below unchanged, where it held for the remainder of the session. Scale-down buying on the part of US roasters helped stem the losses, traders said. Benchmark May futures fell 1.75 cents/lb to close at 171.10 cents/lb, while spot March delivery ended down 2.35 cents/lb at 183.10 cents/lb, after touching contract high of 192 cents early on. Technically May futures would encounter a light resistance at 172.50 cents/lb, followed by 177 cents. Support was noted in the 165.60-166 cents/lb range.

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks fell by 250 bags on February 26 to 25,795 bags. While stocks in New York, San Francisco and Miami remained unchanged, stocks in New Orleans fell by 250 bags.

TURKEY - Coffee imports in April 1996 amounted to 15,283 bags, up on last year's 13,171 bags. This brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1996 (January/April) up to 160,309 bags, sharply up on last year's 61,718 bags. Total imports in 1995 reached 184,164 bags compared to 133,217 bags in 1994. The major supplier of green coffee in January/April 1996 was Brazil with 145,000 bags compared to 50,800 bags in the like period the previous year.

SWEDEN - Coffee imports in July 1996 reached 156,225 bags, up on last year's 134,063 bags. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996 (January/July) up to 1.238 million bags, 34.6 per cent up on the tonnage imported in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 amounted to 1.648 million bags against 1.893 million bags in 1994. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/July 1996 were Colombia (262,200 vs 222,000 bags), Brazil (231,900 vs 254,200 bags) and Guatemala (148,900 vs 95,800 bags). Coffee exports in July 1996 amounted to 13,148 bags, which brought cumulative exports in the first seven months of 1996 up to 127,878 bags against 116,264 bags in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995 reached 204,682 bags against 223,947 bags in 1994. Sweden exports most of its coffee in the form of roast and grounds with the USA (75,900 vs 70,100 bags) and Finland (25,300 vs 16,200 bags) being the main markets.
